sentences.text: This marine reptile reached a length of approximately 6.5 to 7 meters.
The name Kaiwhekea translates to 'squid-eater' from Māori words meaning 'food' and 'squid'.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — was found in 1983 by amateur collector Gary Raper at Shag Point, Otago.
It lay inside a massive concretion weighing an estimated 10 tons.
The skeleton survives mostly as negative moulds because the original mineralized bone was too fragile to keep.
The genus has been classified as an aristonectine plesiosaur closely related to Aristonectes (O'Keefe and Street, 2009), and it belongs to the parent group Weddellonectia.
Other analyses have placed Kaiwhekea within the family Elasmosauridae.
In 2010, Kaiwhekea was transferred to the family Leptocleididae, but recent analyses do not support this placement.

While Kaiwhekea belongs to the parent group Weddellonectia and has been classified within the family Elasmosauridae, it was transferred to the family Leptocleididae in 2010, a placement not supported by recent analyses.
Kaiwhekea is an extinct genus of plesiosaur from the Late Cretaceous of what is now New Zealand.
It lived around 70 to 69 million years ago.
